GJ1.claim: Gujarat has a 1,600 km coastline on the Arabian Sea and is the home state of Mahatma Gandhi.

evidence.quote: boasting a sprawling coastline that spans 1600 kilometres, Gujarat proudly stands as the home state of Mahatma Gandhi, Father of the Nation.

GJ2.claim: Navratri brings Garba and Dandiya dances; the Kutch Rann Utsav is a carnival of crafts and folk music in the desert.

evidence.quote: The vibrant Navratri celebrations, where dance and devotion intertwine, beckon you to partake in the exuberant revelry with dances like Garba and Dandiya.
Experience the Kutch Rann Utsav, a carnival of colours and crafts

GJ3.claim: Gujarati food runs from dhokla and fafda to undhiyu and khandvi, and the Gujarati thali.

evidence.quote: From the sweet notes of Dhokla and Fafda to the spicy delights of Undhiyu and Khandvi
Don’t miss the famous Gujarati thali

GJ4.claim: The Asiatic lions of Gir are Gujarat's great conservation story; the Little Rann of Kutch is a sanctuary for migratory birds.

evidence.quote: The Asiatic lions of Gir National Park stand as a symbol of conservation success
The Little Rann of Kutch, a sanctuary for migratory birds

AMD1.claim: Ahmedabad is India's first UNESCO World Heritage City; Sultan Ahmed Shah founded it in 1411 on the Sabarmati.

evidence.quote: It is India’s first UNESCO World Heritage City, with a living heritage going back a thousand years.
Sultan Ahmed Shah founded Ahmedabad in 1411

AMD2.claim: The Walled City is known for its pols — traditional residential clusters — and over a hundred carved bird-feeding towers called chabutros.

evidence.quote: beckons explorers with its labyrinthine Pols, storied fortifications, and fascinating touches like ‘Chabutros’ – over a hundred elaborately crafted bird-feeding towers.

AMD3.claim: The Uttarayan kite festival fills the sky at Makar Sankranti; Manek Chowk turns into a street-food market after sunset.

evidence.quote: Another highlight on Ahmedabad's festival calendar is the Uttarayan International Kite Festival
Embark on a food tour at Manek Chowk, where the bustling vegetable market transforms into a food haven after sunset.

AMD4.claim: The Sabarmati Riverfront is a 22 km promenade; Kankaria Lake covers 76 acres.

evidence.quote: Discover the essence of Ahmedabad's identity at the Sabarmati Riverfront, where a 22km planned promenade offers stunning views of the Sabarmati River
The artificial lake, shaped like a polygon, covers an area of 76 acres

SAB1.claim: Gandhi set up the Sabarmati Ashram in 1917; it was the starting point of the Dandi March on 12 March 1930, and its grounds span 36 acres.

evidence.quote: With Mahatma Gandhi establishing the Kochrab Ashram in 1915 and the Sabarmati Ashram in 1917
Sabarmati Ashram was the starting point for Gandhi's famous Dandi March, which was launched on March 12, 1930, in protest of the British Salt Law.
The ashram's sprawling grounds, spanning 36 acres

RANN1.claim: The Rann of Kutch is a salt marsh of about 26,000 sq km, split into the Great and Little Rann; in the monsoon it turns into a temporary sea.

evidence.quote: spans roughly 26,000 square kilometres. It is divided into two main parts: the Great Rann of Kutch and the Little Rann of Kutch.
The ethereal beauty of the Rann of Kutch lies in its stark landscape that during the monsoons transforms into a temporary sea.

RANN2.claim: The Rann Utsav festival celebrates local crafts and music; the Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary protects the Little Rann.

evidence.quote: The Rann Utsav, a festival celebrating the local culture, crafts, and music, draws visitors from around the globe.
with sanctuaries like the Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary and the Kutch Desert Wildlife Sanctuary

RANN3.claim: Kalo Dungar, north of Khavda, is Kutch's highest point at 462 m, with views over the Great Rann.

evidence.quote: North of the village of Khavda, Kalo Dungar (Black Hill) marks Kutch’s highest point (462 m)

RANN4.claim: Kutch's Rabari herders live in round bhoongas; Rogan lacquer painting is a speciality of Niruna village near Bhuj.

evidence.quote: Among them are the Rabaris, whose round houses (bhoongas) with conical roofs are a distinctive feature of the Kutch landscape.
Rogan, a specialty of Niruna village near Bhuj

DHO1.claim: Dholavira, on Khadir Bet island in the Great Rann, is one of the five largest Harappan sites; it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.

evidence.quote: It is one of the five largest Harappan sites
It is located on Khadir Bet island in the Kutch Desert Wildlife Sanctuary in the Great Rann of Kutch .
Designated 2021 (44th session )

DHO2.claim: Winter is the best time to visit the Rann; Khadir Bet has no public transport, so come with a car or taxi.

evidence.quote: Note that there is no public transport in Khadir Bet. It is best to have a car or taxi at your disposal.
Winter is definitely the best time to visit any place in the Rann of Kutch.

PAT1.claim: Patan, once Anhilwad Patan, grew on the Saraswati and was the seat of the Solankis; the Salvi family has woven Patola saris here for over 700 years.

evidence.quote: Known in earlier times as Anhilwad Patan, the city grew along the banks of the Saraswati River
The tradition has been preserved by the Salvi family, who brought this art form to Patan more than 700 years ago.

PAT2.claim: The Modhera Sun Temple is 25 km from Patan; Ahmedabad airport is about 130 km away and Mehsana station about 30 km.

evidence.quote: Just 25 kilometres away stands the Modhera Sun Temple
By Air: Ahmedabad Airport, approximately 130 km away
By Rail: Mehsana Railway Station, located around 30 km from Patan

RKV1.claim: Rani ki Vav was commissioned in 1063 CE by Queen Udayamati in memory of King Bhimdev I; built as an inverted temple, it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014.

evidence.quote: Rani Ki Vav was commissioned in 1063 CE by Queen Udayamati of the Chaulukya dynasty in memory of her husband, King Bhimdev I.
Rani Ki Vav was designed in the form of an inverted temple.
In 2014, Rani Ki Vav was inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List

RKV2.claim: Visit October to March; buses from Ahmedabad take about 3.5 hours.

evidence.quote: The most pleasant time to visit Rani Ki Vav is between October and March
Intercity buses operate regularly from Ahmedabad and the journey takes around 3.5 hours.

SOU1.claim: The Statue of Unity at Kevadia honours Sardar Patel; at 182 m it is the world's tallest statue, inaugurated on 31 October 2018, 100 km south-east of Vadodara.

evidence.quote: At a towering height of 182 meters, the Statue of Unity in Kevadia is a monument that has no parallel in the world.
On 31 October 2018, coinciding with the 143rd anniversary of Patel's birth, the statue was inaugurated.
100 kilometres (62 miles) southeast of the city of Vadodara

SOU2.claim: Lifts climb to a viewing gallery at 153 m in just over 30 seconds; a laser light-and-sound show runs nightly.

evidence.quote: the third zone leads to the viewing gallery at a height of 153 meters
Ascending to the viewing gallery takes just over 30 seconds
the laser light and sound show, a nightly spectacle at the Statue of Unity

SOU3.claim: Open 8 am to 6 pm; closed Mondays.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 08:00 AM
Closing time - 06:00 PM
(Closed on Mondays)

SOM1.claim: The Somnath Temple at Prabhas Patan, on the Arabian Sea, is regarded as the first of the twelve Jyotirlingas.

evidence.quote: Standing majestically on the shores of the Arabian Sea at Prabhas Patan in Gujarat's Gir Somnath district
Regarded as the first among the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva

SOM2.claim: A sound-and-light show runs in the complex; October to February is the best time, and the temple is open all year.

evidence.quote: Visitors can also attend the sound-and-light show held within the temple complex
The most pleasant time to visit Somnath Temple is between October and February
The temple remains open throughout the year

GIR1.claim: Gir is the only place outside Africa where lions roam wild; declared a sanctuary in 1965, it covers 1,412 sq km.

evidence.quote: Gir is the only place in the world outside Africa where lions live and roam freely in the wild.
Declared a wildlife sanctuary in 1965, Gir stretches over 1,412 square kilometers

GIR2.claim: Besides lions, Gir has leopards, striped hyenas, the four-horned chowsingha and 425+ bird species.

evidence.quote: including leopards, jackals, striped hyenas, and Indian foxes
A staggering 425+ bird species

GIR3.claim: Winter (16 Oct–Feb) safaris run 6:45–9:45 am and 3–6 pm; summer (1 Mar–15 Jun) 6–9 am and 3–6 pm.

evidence.quote: Morning 06:45 AM to 09:45 AM, afternoon 03:00 PM to 06:00 PM
Morning 06:00 AM to 09:00 AM, and afternoon 03:00 PM to 06:00 PM

DWK1.claim: Dwarka on the Arabian Sea is one of the four Char Dham sites; Beyt Dwarka is a short boat ride away, and Nageshwar is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas.

evidence.quote: for Dwarka is one of the four sacred Hindu pilgrimage sites called the Char Dham.
A short boat ride away lies Beyt Dwarka
Pay homage at the revered Nageshwar Jyotirlinga

DWK2.claim: November to February is the best time to visit Dwarka.

evidence.quote: Dwarka is at its most incredible during the winter, from November to February

DWT1.claim: The five-storey Dwarkadhish Temple, reached by 56 steps, takes its present form from the 16th century.

evidence.quote: Venture 56 steps up the small hill, and you will see the Dwarkadhish temple in all its glory.
you'll be awe-struck by the grandeur of its towering, five-story edifice
ultimately achieving its current grandeur that dates to the 16th century
Opening time - 06:30 AM to 01:00 PM and 05:00 PM to 09:30 PM

CHA1.claim: Champaner, at the foot of Pavagadh Hill, was Gujarat's capital under Sultan Mahmud Begada; its archaeological park of mosques, temples, forts and stepwells is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

evidence.quote: Once the capital of Gujarat under the reign of Sultan Mahmud Begada
At the heart lies the Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

CHA2.claim: Trek or take the cable car up to the Kalika Mata Temple on Pavagadh Hill.

evidence.quote: Begin with a trek or cable car ride to the Kalika Mata Temple, at the top of Pavagadh Hill

MP1.claim: Madhya Pradesh is called the 'Tiger State of India', with Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Panna, Pench and Satpura.

evidence.quote: Madhya Pradesh is also called the ‘Tiger State of India,’
sanctuaries like Panna National Park, Bandhavgarh National Park, Kanha National Park, and Pench National Park

MP2.claim: Its UNESCO sites include the Khajuraho temples, Sanchi and the Bhimbetka rock shelters; Omkareshwar's Jyotirlinga sits on a Narmada island.

evidence.quote: From the intricate carvings of Khajuraho Group of Monuments, a UNESCO World Heritage Si
Seated on an island formed by the Narmada River, the Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga Temple draws devotees and seekers alike.

KHA1.claim: Khajuraho was the Chandela capital from the 9th to the 12th century; of 85 temples said to have been built, 20 survive, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

evidence.quote: From the 9th to the 12th century AD, Khajuraho flourished as the capital of the powerful Chandela dynasty
Local legends say that the Chandelas built a staggering 85 temples in Khajuraho
This UNESCO World Heritage Site is a must-see destination for history enthusiasts and art lovers alike.

KHA2.claim: Khajuraho Airport is 3 km south of the town.

evidence.quote: The airport is 3 km south of Khajuraho

KHA3.claim: The Khajuraho Dance Festival is held from the last week of February into March.

evidence.quote: Every year in the last week of February to March, the temple celebrates the Khajuraho dance festival.

KMT1.claim: The Kandariya Mahadev Temple, built by King Vidyadhar about 1025–1050 AD, is the largest temple at Khajuraho, over 31 m high with more than 870 sculptures.

evidence.quote: King Vidyadhar from the Chandel Dynasty constructed this beautiful Mahadev Temple between 1025- 1050 AD.
this is also the largest temple in that vicinity
with its multiple towers reaching over 31 meters high! Over 870 sculptures adorn

ORC1.claim: Orchha on the Betwa river was founded by Rudra Pratap Singh in the 15th century; its fort complex holds the Raj Mahal, Sheesh Mahal and Jahangir Mahal.

evidence.quote: Rudra Pratap Singh founded the kingdom of Orchha in the 15th century
At its heart, the Orchha Fort complex has three magnificent palaces.

ORC2.claim: The 14 cenotaphs of the Bundela rulers stand on the Betwa; the Laxmi Narayan Temple has well-preserved murals.

evidence.quote: The Bundela dynasty's 14 cenotaphs are located on the banks of the river Betwa.
It features well-preserved murals inside and offers fantastic views from the climbable roof.

ORC3.claim: Orchha Fort is open daily from sunrise to sunset; a light-and-sound show follows in the evening.

evidence.quote: Opening time - The Orchha Fort is open daily from sunrise to sunset.
After the fort closes its gates, the nightly light and sound spectacle c

RRM1.claim: At the Ram Raja Mandir, built by Madhukar Shah Bundela in the 16th century, Rama is worshipped as a king; it is open from sunrise to sunset.

evidence.quote: Established by Madhukar Shah Bundela of Bundela kingdom in 16th century India
Opening time - Ram Raja Mandir in Orchha is open for visitors from sunrise to sunset, every day of the week.

GWL1.claim: Gwalior is the birthplace of the singer Tansen; its Chaturbhuj Temple carries the world's first written zero. October to March is the best time.

evidence.quote: Etched on the stones of its Chaturbhuj Temple is the world's first occurrence of zero as a written number!
This city is also the birthplace of Tansen
the best time to visit is between October and March

GWL2.claim: The Jai Vilas Palace is a museum with grand chandeliers; the Bateshwar temples, about 200 in sandstone, lie 35 km north.

evidence.quote: Step into a world of luxurious living with Jai Vilas Palace.
a complex of around 200 temples carved in sandstone, dating from the 8 th to 10 th centuries

GWF1.claim: Gwalior Fort, spread over 3 sq km, dates back to the 6th century; Raja Man Singh Tomar built the Man Mandir Palace, and the Teli ka Mandir is its oldest monument.

evidence.quote: Spread across three square kilometres
this architectural marvel traces its origins back to the 6th century
Built by Raja Man Singh Tomar
climb to the Teli ka Mandir, the fort's oldest monument
Opening time - 06:00 AM
Closing time - 05:30 PM

BHO1.claim: Bhopal was ruled by the Begums from 1819 to 1926; the Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Manav Sangrahalaya is India's largest anthropological museum, on 200 acres.

evidence.quote: Bhopal thrived under the rule of powerful Begums, female leaders who reigned from 1819 to 1926.
India's largest anthropological museum! Spread across a sprawling 200-acre landscape

BHI1.claim: Bhimbetka, 45 km from Bhopal, is a UNESCO site of over 750 rock shelters on seven hills, with paintings up to 30,000 years old.

evidence.quote: A UNESCO World Heritage Site that consists of seven hills and over 750 rock shelters distributed over 10 km
Located 45 kms from Bhopal
With paintings up to 30,000 years old
Opening time - 07:00 AM
Closing time - 06:00 PM

SAN1.claim: The Sanchi Stupa, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was first built in the 3rd century BCE on Emperor Ashoka's orders.

evidence.quote: Designated a UNESCO World Heritage site and widely revered as the source of Buddhist architecture
Mauryan Emperor Ashoka ordered its construction
Opening time - 08:00 AM
Closing time - 06:30 PM

UJJ1.claim: Ujjain, on the Shipra, is a major pilgrimage city for Shaivites, Vaishnavites and Shaktas.

evidence.quote: Ujjain continues to be an important place of pilgrimage for Shaivites , Vaishnavites and Shaktas .

MAH1.claim: Mahakaleshwar is the only Jyotirlinga that faces south; its Bhasma Aarti begins every morning at 4.

evidence.quote: it is the only Jyotirlinga that faces south, known as dakshinamukhi
Beginning every morning at 4, this ritual is performed to awaken Lord Shiva.

MAH2.claim: Darshan is open 4 am to 11 pm.

evidence.quote: Darshans are open from 04:00 AM to 11:00 PM

KAN1.claim: Kanha, in the Maikal range of the Satpuras, is one of India's largest tiger reserves and saved the hard-ground barasingha from extinction.

evidence.quote: Kanha National Park is one of India's largest and most storied tiger reserves
Kanha's defining achievement is saving the hard-ground barasingha (swamp deer), the state animal of Madhya Pradesh, from the edge of extinction.

KAN2.claim: Kanha opens mid-October to the end of June; safaris run in the Kanha, Kisli, Mukki and Sarhi zones, booked on the forest department portal. Jabalpur airport is about 137 km away.

evidence.quote: The park is open from mid-October to the end of June .
Bookings are made through the Madhya Pradesh forest department's online portal
Kanha National Park is conveniently accessible from Jabalpur Airport which is approx. 137 km away

BAN1.claim: Bandhavgarh in Umaria district has the highest density of Bengal tigers of any reserve; the old Bandhavgarh Fort stands at its heart.

evidence.quote: is renowned for having the highest density of Royal Bengal tigers of any reserve in the world
The park takes its name from the roughly 2,000-year-old Bandhavgarh Fort at its heart

BAN2.claim: Safaris run in the Tala, Magdhi and Khitauli zones; book ahead. Umaria station is about 32 km away.

evidence.quote: Tiger safaris across the Tala, Magdhi, and Khitauli zones
advance booking is essential
The nearest railway station is Umaria , located about 32 km from the park

DHU1.claim: At Bhedaghat, 20–30 km from Jabalpur, the Narmada drops about 30 m at Dhuandhar Falls; upstream it cuts through the Marble Rocks, with cliffs up to 100 feet.

evidence.quote: About 20–30 km from Jabalpur, at a spot called Bhedaghat, the Narmada river narrows and plunges roughly 30 metres into a gorge
a gorge where sheer white marble cliffs, some rising 100 feet, flank the river for several kilometres

DHU2.claim: The 10th-century Chausath Yogini Temple stands on a hill above Bhedaghat.

evidence.quote: The 10th-century Chausath Yogini Temple, perched on a hill above Bhedaghat with panoramic river views.

PAC1.claim: Pachmarhi, Madhya Pradesh's only hill station at about 1,100 m in the Satpuras, lies in a UNESCO biosphere reserve (2009) and the Satpura Tiger Reserve.

evidence.quote: The only hill station in Madhya Pradesh, Pachmarhi sits at around 1,100 metres in a valley of the Satpura Range
Pachmarhi sits entirely within the Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve, added to UNESCO's list of Biosphere Reserves in 2009

PAC2.claim: See Bee Falls (about 150 ft), the Jata Shankar caves and Priyadarshini Point; Itarsi junction is about 150 km away.

evidence.quote: Bee Falls (Jamuna Prapat): a roughly 150-foot cascading waterfall
Jata Shankar Caves: a sacred cave shrine linked to a Shiva legend
An alternative railhead is Itarsi Junction (ET) , situated around 150 km away

overview.text:
Gujarat runs along a 1,600 km Arabian Sea coast and is the home state of Mahatma Gandhi. Ahmedabad was India's first UNESCO World Heritage City; Gir is the last home of the Asiatic lion; the white Rann of Kutch and Harappan Dholavira lie in the far west.

Pilgrims come for Somnath — first of the twelve Jyotirlingas — and Dwarka, one of the Char Dham.

body.intro: Gir is the only place outside Africa to see wild lions.

sections.heading: Why Gir
sections.text: Declared a sanctuary in 1965, Gir covers 1,412 sq km and is the last home of the Asiatic lion.

items.title: Summer (1 Mar–15 Jun)

sections.text: Somnath, the first Jyotirlinga, is close by on the coast.

body.intro: Khajuraho is one of India's great temple sites — give it a full day.

sections.heading: The temples
sections.text: Khajuraho was the Chandela capital from the 9th to the 12th century; 20 temples survive, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sections.heading: Kandariya Mahadev
sections.text: The largest temple, built about 1025–1050 AD, over 31 m high with more than 870 sculptures.

sections.heading: When and how
sections.text: The dance festival runs from the last week of February into March; the airport is 3 km from town.

body.intro: Madhya Pradesh is India's Tiger State — here's how to pick a park.

sections.heading: Kanha
sections.text: One of India's largest tiger reserves; saved the barasingha. Open mid-October to the end of June; safaris in Kanha, Kisli, Mukki and Sarhi.

sections.heading: Bandhavgarh
sections.text: The highest density of Bengal tigers of any reserve; Tala, Magdhi and Khitauli zones. Book ahead.

sections.heading: Satpura and Pachmarhi
sections.text: Pachmarhi lies in a UNESCO biosphere reserve and the Satpura Tiger Reserve.
